notes_language_policy.teaching: Simple natural Telugu explaining the concept
notes_language_policy.technical_terms: Use familiar English exam terms beside Telugu, including mass,size,diameter,volume,density,temperature,dwarf planet,Hawking radiation. Do not rely on obscure Telugu translations alone.
notes_language_policy.quantities_and_units: Standard scientific symbols such as kg,km,g/cm³,°C,K,AU; e.g.1.99 ×10³⁰ kg. Clearly state whether an Earth comparison is mass or volume.
notes_language_policy.mcqs: Later: separate complete Telugu and complete English versions; question wording/options/keys remain unchanged during notes editing.
notes_language_policy.cause_and_effect: Name the cause and result explicitly. Avoid ambiguous phrases such as వేడి నీటిని. Separate Photosynthesis,Evaporation,Winds,Water cycle. Atmosphere means the gas envelope;Weather means conditions at a place/time.
notes_language_policy.table_definitions: Technical English must appear in the definition cell itself where needed, even if the row heading already has English. Use full phrases such as gravitational effects,reflected starlight,atmospheric entry,parallax and differential rotation. Audit inflected Telugu phrases, not just exact root-word matches.
notes_language_policy.planet_presentation: Define Rocky/Terrestrial,Gas giant,Ice giant before use. Present comparable planet colours,surface,atmosphere,rings,moons and special properties in tables; give short causal explanations beside them. Avoid repeated bracket labels on ordinary words.

visual_policy.freeze: Freeze each chapter before visual production; do not wait for the full book. Reopen the freeze if a material correction is needed.
visual_policy.accuracy: Prefer editable SVG for measured geometry and labels. Use raster illustrations only where helpful. Diagrams must declare scale, legend, reference and schematic exaggeration where relevant.
visual_policy.assessment: Map each visual to concepts, questions and exact note anchors; do not duplicate questions merely by changing decoration.
visual_policy.presentation: Recreate useful boxes and comparison tables using original layouts; group comparable properties rather than fragmented individual paragraphs. Keep concept explanations next to the comparison.
visual_policy.revision_infographics: Create polished, original overview infographics after each chapter freeze; use clear contrast and visual hierarchy, preserve references/units, link every panel to notes and existing MCQs, and never count decorative repetitions as new questions.

mandatory_manual_editorial_rule.scope: Every geography chapter, uploaded source page, note, MCQ, translation and explanation, including revisions of existing work
requirements: Manually read every source sentence and printed fact/concept in context; ignore handwriting as previously instructed.
Manually compose every teaching sentence and each language version; use natural Telugu explanations and English technical terms in notes, separate complete Telugu and English MCQs.
Manually reread and review every final sentence in context for meaning, clarity, prerequisites, accuracy and natural language.
Use subheadings and connected explanations. Keep tables for meaningful comparisons or reference data; do not mechanically convert cells into paragraphs.
Preserve source facts, documented corrections, stable IDs, scoring holds and exact section links.
Do not declare a chapter manually reviewed or complete until its entire final text has received this sentence-by-sentence review. Report partial work honestly.
prohibited: Batch word substitution or glossary replacement as a substitute for authoring or review

Automated structural tests presented as evidence of manual editorial review
allowed_automation: Save or format text already manually authored and reviewed
Read/extract/render source files to support manual reading; extraction is not a substitute for reading
Check hashes, preservation, duplicate IDs, language leakage, answer keys, links and navigation
